extracted.intended_audience: researchers applying for NIH/NICHD K-series career development awards (senior postdoctoral fellows and early-career faculty)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and requirements for preparing and submitting NIH/NICHD Career Development (K) award applications, covering mechanism-specific purpose, eligibility, institutional/institute-specific requirements, and procedural resources. Intended to help applicants determine eligibility and which parent announcement/instructions to follow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program objective — independence and competitiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: The objective of these programs is to bring candidates to the point where they are able to conduct their research independently and are competitive for major grant support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications and proposed career development plans should demonstrate a clear pathway toward research independence and competitiveness for major grants. This program-level objective applies across K mechanisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citizenship/residency requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Current NIH policies require that, by the time of the award, applicants must be U.S. citizens, non-citizen U.S. nationals, or have been lawfully admitted for permanent residence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requirement applies to all the mechanisms on this NICHD page EXCEPT the K99/R00. Applicants must ensure their immigration status meets this requirement at the time of award.

rubrics_metrics.name: K01 — Mentored Research Scientist Development Award (purpose and scope)
rubrics_metrics.description: Supports 3 to 5 years of mentored research training experience in the biomedical, behavioral, or clinical sciences. NICHD accepts K01 applications for only three research areas: Rehabilitation Research, Child Abuse and Neglect, and Population Research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants to NICHD K01 must propose 3–5 years of mentored training within one of the three accepted NICHD research areas and meet the degree eligibility below. Use the appropriate parent K01 announcement variant depending on clinical trial status.

rubrics_metrics.name: K01 — Eligibility (degree requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Eligibility: Those with a research or health professional doctorate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should confirm they hold an acceptable doctoral degree as specified in the parent announcement and NICHD IC-specific table.

rubrics_metrics.name: K08 — Mentored Clinical Scientist Research Career Development Award (purpose)
rubrics_metrics.description: Supports 'protected time' for an intensive, supervised research career development experience in the fields of biomedical and behavioral research, including translational research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should demonstrate protected research time and an intensive, supervised career development plan appropriate for clinical investigators. Select the correct parent K08 announcement based on clinical trial involvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: K08 — Eligibility (degree requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Eligibility: Those with a clinical doctorate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must hold a clinical doctoral degree (MD, DO, DDS, DVM, etc.) as defined in the parent announcement and NICHD-specific information.

rubrics_metrics.name: K23 — Mentored Patient-Oriented Research Career Development Award (purpose)
rubrics_metrics.description: Supports 3 to 5 years of mentored research training experience in patient-oriented research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should propose a mentored training plan focused on patient-oriented research for 3–5 years and use the appropriate parent announcement variant for clinical trial status.

rubrics_metrics.name: K23 — Eligibility (degree requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Eligibility: Those with a health professional doctorate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm that your degree meets the 'health professional doctorate' definition in the parent announcement and NICHD IC-specific guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: K25 — Mentored Quantitative Research Development Award (purpose)
rubrics_metrics.description: Aims to attract to NIH-relevant research those investigators whose quantitative science and engineering research has thus far not been focused primarily on questions of health and disease.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should explain the transition of quantitative/engineering expertise toward NIH-relevant health research and justify the mentored development plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: K25 — Eligibility (degree and disciplinary background)
rubrics_metrics.description: Eligibility: Those with a research or health professional doctorate and a background in engineering or quantitative sciences (e.g., mathematics, statistics, economics, computer science, imaging science, informatics, physics, or chemistry).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must document quantitative/engineering backgrounds and how their skills will be applied to health-related research.

rubrics_metrics.name: K99/R00 — Pathway to Independence (purpose and two-stage structure)
rubrics_metrics.description: Two-stage award to support the final stages of postdoctoral training and to provide independent funding when the candidate secures a faculty position. This award aims to increase and maintain a strong cohort of new and talented NIH-supported independent investigators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications must address both the mentored (K99) and independent (R00) phases and show readiness for transition to independence. Select the correct parent announcement version depending on clinical trial status.

rubrics_metrics.name: K99/R00 — Eligibility (degree and postdoctoral time limit)
rubrics_metrics.description: Eligibility: Those with a clinical or research doctorate and no more than 4 years of postdoctoral research training at the time of initial application or resubmission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must carefully calculate and document postdoctoral time to ensure they do not exceed the 4-year limit at application/resubmission.

rubrics_metrics.name: NICHD-specific information requirement (Table of IC-Specific Information)
rubrics_metrics.description: Select the 'Table of IC-Specific Information, Requirements, and Staff Contacts' link within the parent announcement to find NICHD-specific information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each parent announcement contains an IC-specific table — applicants must consult that NICHD table for institute-specific application details, requirements, and contact information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parent announcement variant selection by clinical trial involvement
rubrics_metrics.description: Each K mechanism points to three parent announcement variants: (Clinical Trial Not Allowed), (Clinical Trial Required), and (Basic Experimental Studies in Humans Required).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must pick the correct parent announcement variant that matches whether their proposed work includes a clinical trial or basic experimental studies in humans; use the appropriate instructions and policy text for that variant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application instruction set requirement — use 'Career Development Instructions'
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants for Career Development Awards (K-series) should use the 'Career Development Instructions' within the NIH application instruction sets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the Career Development-specific application forms and formatting instructions rather than other NIH instruction sets to ensure compliance with submission requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer review jurisdiction — Scientific Review Branch (SRB)
rubrics_metrics.description: The NICHD Scientific Review Branch reviews applications for career development awards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should be aware that NICHD SRB conducts peer review; the page also provides access to review panel rosters. Ensure proposals address typical NIH review considerations (significance, investigators, innovation, approach, environment) consistent with NIH review practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIH Grants Policy Statement (GPS) applicability — Chapter 12
rubrics_metrics.description: The GPS outlines policies for all grant mechanisms at NIH, including fellowships, career development awards, and institutional training grants. Career Development (K) Award policies are in Chapter 12.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For policy questions and post-award requirements, consult the GPS Chapter 12 as the authoritative policy source.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resources and supporting materials (FAQs, sample applications, forms, contacts)
rubrics_metrics.description: The NICHD page links to FAQs about K awards, sample applications, forms, contacts for NICHD funding information, and other resources for applicants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should review FAQs, sample applications, and required forms and contact NICHD extramural staff as needed to prepare compliant and competitive applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institute participation note — K02 and K24
rubrics_metrics.description: IMPORTANT NOTE: NICHD no longer participates in the K02 or K24 programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants seeking K02 or K24 support should not apply to NICHD for those mechanisms and should consult other ICs if interested in those award types.
